reasons.correctness: SupportTicketCreatedEventListener#onTicketCreated uses plain @EventListener. It runs synchronously inside createTicket's transaction, so the e-mail still goes out before commit and on rollback. The task is not fixed; the hidden tests pass only because they call the listener directly.
reasons.convention_fit: The listener lacks @TransactionalEventListener(phase = TransactionPhase.AFTER_COMMIT), which the side-effect convention requires. Constructor injection, the feature package support/ticket/event and the catch-and-log are compliant.
reasons.design_fit: The event/listener split is the right shape, but a plain listener keeps the side effect inside the transaction and on the rollback path. That is the structural defect the task exists to remove.
reasons.test_quality: SupportTicketCreatedEventListenerUnitTest covers the send path and the swallowed failure with MockitoExtension. No test verifies that createTicket publishes the event instead of calling EmailService. Nothing pins the after-commit phase.
reasons.graph_use: The only graph query was a generic `MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.file_path LIMIT 1`, which located nothing relevant. The agent then read an unrelated event class, not an existing listener, and edited directly.
